name: Blackjack
author: ChuckBuilds
description: Deals one hand of Las Vegas blackjack per rotation. Cards slide in and flip face up a few seconds apart, the player follows basic strategy, the dealer plays the house rules, and the hand ends on a BLACKJACK! / BUST! / PUSH banner. Every hand comes off a real shuffled shoe, so no two rotations are the same.

versions.notes: Vegas marquee support, as STATIC only. A plugin that declares no Vegas mode is not skipped by the marquee -- it has one frame of its display() captured and scrolled past, which for a clock is right and for a twenty-second hand is a single frozen still, often a card halfway through its slide. STATIC pauses the marquee and lets the hand play. SCROLL and FIXED_SEGMENT are not offered because both want the content handed over as an image to be moved, and a hand is not an image; offering a vegas_mode override would only let someone pick the frozen frame.

Initial release. One hand of blackjack per rotation off a persistent multi-deck shoe, played by Vegas basic strategy against a dealer who stands on soft 17 by default. Four-colour deck (red hearts, gold diamonds, green clubs, indigo spades) on a lit felt table -- an ordered dither against a radial falloff, so the weave is densest under the cards and thins to black at the edges -- with a crimson-and-gold card back. Each seat reads as one line: name, hand, total. Rare hands announce themselves on the result banner (777, 21 IN 3, CHARLIE, DEALER n, BOTH 21, and a session win streak) before the score counts up. The deal, the hole-card reveal, a bust and a natural each get a beat of their own, and a hand ends with a tinted flash, a rattle and a spark burst on a win -- all of it a pure function of elapsed time, with no animation state anywhere. Card faces are a centred 5x7 rank at every size a real panel produces, with a pip-count sprite tier held back for cards larger than any of them, because counting pips across a room is slower than reading a numeral. The table lays itself out from the panel shape rather than a size whitelist, stacked normally and dealer-left/player-right on strips wider than 5:1. Dynamic duration is on by default, so the rotation lasts exactly as long as the hand does.
